text_blocks.snippet: PCR tests and rapid antigen tests are the two main types of COVID-19 tests. PCR tests are generally more accurate and sensitive, detecting even small amounts of the virus, but results can take a few days. Rapid antigen tests are less sensitive but provide results much faster, often within minutes. The best test for you depends on your specific needs and circumstances.
snippet_highlighted_words: PCR tests are generally more accurate and sensitive, detecting even small amounts of the virus, but results can take a few days.
Rapid antigen tests are less sensitive but provide results much faster, often within minutes

list.snippet: How they work: PCR tests detect the virus's genetic material (RNA) by amplifying it, making it detectable even in very low concentrations.
Accuracy: Highly accurate and considered the gold standard for detecting COVID-19.
Turnaround time: Results can take a few days, as they are typically processed in a lab.
Best for: Diagnosing COVID-19 early in the course of illness, especially when symptoms are mild.
Considerations: May stay positive for weeks after the infection has passed, even if you are no longer contagious.
How they work: Rapid tests detect specific proteins (antigens) on the surface of the virus.
Accuracy: Less sensitive than PCR tests, meaning they may not detect the virus if the viral load is low.
Turnaround time: Results are usually available within minutes.
Best for: Quickly identifying individuals who are likely to be highly infectious.
Considerations: May miss some infections, especially early in the course of illness or when symptoms are mild.
